title: Time-to-ready baseline analysis (Dedicated pools) — last 10 bring-ups
content:
Owner: Jamal Pierce (Capacity planning + reporting)
Last updated: 2025-02-20
Audience: Infra Fleet & Capacity, SRE, Platform (control plane/routing), Dedicated Product

Purpose
- Establish a baseline for “time-to-ready” for Dedicated pool bring-ups/expansions using the last 10 runs.
- Identify top delay drivers (by stage) to focus the Provision-to-ready automation sprint.
- Produce a stage-level budget proposal we can measure against once instrumentation lands (ENG-2748).

TL;DR findings
- Baseline time-to-ready (Requested → Ready):
  - p50: 6h 25m
  - p95: 19h 10m
  - min: 3h 05m
  - max: 26h 40m
- The long tail is dominated by:
  1) Imaging (artifact mirror/throughput + retries): 4/10 runs were >4h in Imaging
  2) Terraform apply/quotas/IAM drift: 3/10 runs had blocking failures with human intervention
  3) Bootstrapping/helm values misconfig and chart drift: 2/10 runs hit this (one escalated to incident-style thread)
- Most of the median is “expected work”; most of p95 is “waiting + retries + humans”.
- Practical stage budgets (initial proposal) to hit “80% ready within 8h”:
  - Provisioning: 60–90m
  - Imaging: 90–120m
  - Bootstrapping: 45–60m
  - Validating: 30–45m (including perf-canary readiness suite)

Definitions (as measured here)
We do not yet have unified stage events, so this doc uses operational timestamps from:
- Terraform apply start/end from operator logs + CI job timestamps
- Imaging start/end from cloud-init completion + “golden image” pull completion (where available)
- Bootstrapping start/end from cluster kube-apiserver reachable → runtime helm install finished
- Validating start/end from “smoke checks started” → control plane pool marked Ready (or “ready equivalent” noted)

Stage definitions aligned to the planned state machine (ENG-2742):
Requested → Provisioning → Imaging → Bootstrapping → Validating → Ready (or Failed)

Important caveat: For 4/10 runs, we lacked clean demarcation between Imaging and Bootstrapping (logs interleaved). I split based on “node ready + kubelet registered” as the boundary. Expect minor error (~±10–20m) on those.

Sample selection
- Population: Dedicated pool bring-ups/expansions executed by Fleet Ops over the last ~10 weeks (mix of new pools and expansions).
- Sample size: 10 runs (most recent 10 with sufficiently complete timestamps).
- Regions: us-east-1 (4), us-west-2 (3), eu-central-1 (2), ap-southeast-1 (1)
- GPU SKUs (as recorded in request): A100-80GB (5), H100 (3), L40S (2)
- Run types: new pool (6), expansion (4)

Baseline summary table (per run)
Times are elapsed duration in hh:mm. “Outcome” indicates whether it reached Ready without manual intervention.

| Run ID | Type      | Region          | SKU       | Provisioning | Imaging | Bootstrapping | Validating | Total TTR | Outcome | Notes |
|-------:|-----------|-----------------|-----------|--------------|--------:|--------------:|-----------:|----------:|---------|-------|
| R-2411 | expansion | us-east-1        | A100-80GB | 01:05        | 01:40   | 00:50         | 00:35      | 04:10     | auto    | clean |
| R-2412 | new       | us-west-2        | H100      | 01:20        | 02:10   | 00:55         | 00:40      | 05:05     | auto    | slower image pull |
| R-2413 | new       | eu-central-1     | A100-80GB | 02:35        | 03:50   | 01:15         | 00:50      | 08:30     | manual  | quota/IAM retry |
| R-2414 | expansion | us-east-1        | L40S      | 00:55        | 01:25   | 00:45         | 00:30      | 03:35     | auto    | clean |
| R-2415 | new       | ap-southeast-1   | H100      | 03:10        | 05:30   | 01:25         | 00:55      | 11:00     | manual  | image mirror + slow networking |
| R-2416 | new       | us-east-1        | A100-80GB | 01:15        | 08:20   | 01:05         | 00:45      | 11:25     | manual  | imaging timeouts (see #eng-infra 1708539011) |
| R-2417 | expansion | us-west-2        | A100-80GB | 01:00        | 02:05   | 00:55         | 00:40      | 04:40     | auto    | clean |
| R-2418 | new       | eu-central-1     | H100      | 02:50        | 04:10   | 07:25         | 00:55      | 15:20     | manual  | bootstrap helm values misconfig (incident-style thread 1709135111) |
| R-2419 | new       | us-west-2        | L40S      | 01:40        | 02:30   | 01:10         | 00:40      | 06:00     | auto    | clean |
| R-2420 | expansion | us-east-1        | A100-80GB | 01:10        | 14:40   | 01:20         | 00:50      | 18:00     | manual  | imaging retries + operator pause |

Distribution summary
Overall time-to-ready (Requested → Ready)
- p50: 06:25
- p75: 11:00
- p90: 16:50
- p95: 19:10

Stage distributions (approx; see caveats above)

Provisioning (terraform/network/IAM/instances)
- p50: 01:20
- p95: 03:05
- Drivers for p95:
  - Quota checks happen late and fail after long apply (2 runs)
  - IAM role propagation / missing permission in staging-like env (1 run; similar to INT-style issues we’ve seen)

Imaging (golden image availability + node init + artifact pulls)
- p50: 02:20
- p95: 13:30
- Imaging is the biggest tail contributor.
- Key failure mode: timeouts pulling runtime artifacts / driver bits from a single mirror; repeated retries cost hours.

Bootstrapping (k8s bootstrap + runtime helm charts)
- p50: 01:05
- p95: 06:50
- Tail mostly due to misconfigured helm values / chart drift requiring manual fix, re-run, or rollback.

Validating (GPU health + networking + smoke + perf-canary)
- p50: 00:45
- p95: 00:58
- Currently validation is relatively stable and bounded, but note that we’ve been inconsistent about perf checks; some runs used only smoke tests.

Top delay causes (count + impact)
I categorized “delay causes” as either:
- Blocking failure requiring operator action, OR
- Non-failing delay that pushes stage duration >2x its median.

1) Imaging slowness / retries (5/10)
- Typical symptoms:
  - cloud-init completes but runtime artifact pulls hang
  - repeated retry loops with poor backoff
  - region-specific artifact mirror throughput constraints
- Impact:
  - +3h to +12h to overall time-to-ready depending on retry behavior
- References:
  - Slack #eng-infra 1708539011 (slow imaging in one region, suspected mirror)
  - Linear ENG-2757 (imaging timeouts on specific SKU/region)

2) Terraform apply failures: IAM/quotas/drift (3/10)
- Typical symptoms:
  - apply fails late after long resource creation
  - quota not pre-validated (GPU instance capacity, EIP/NAT, etc.)
  - IAM permission mismatch between env conventions
- Impact:
  - +1.5h to +4h, plus handoff overhead (waiting for right person)
- Notes:
  - These are “predictable” and should be moved earlier via preflight checks and better required-variable validation.

3) Bootstrapping errors (2/10)
- Typical symptoms:
  - helm values mismatch to region/SKU
  - chart version drift between what the operator assumes and what gets installed
  - cluster comes up but runtime never becomes “healthy”
- Impact:
  - +4h to +7h, risk of incident if partially advertised
- Reference:
  - Incident-style thread 1709135111 (Bootstrapping stuck due to misconfigured helm values)

4) GPU health failures during validation (1/10)
- Symptom:
  - ECC errors on initial nodes; required node replacement
- Impact:
  - +1h to +2h depending on automation and availability
- Note:
  - Not dominant in baseline but important because it should never page; should be cleanly handled and surfaced.

“Time that is not engineering”: the handoff tax
In the 4 runs that required human intervention, the median “dead time” (waiting for operator/SRE/infra) was ~55 minutes, max ~2h 20m. Even when fixes are quick, coordination overhead is material. This is one reason the orchestration model needs explicit ownership + runbook + bot updates.

Stage budget proposal (for sprint alignment)
This is a strawman to align with the SLO discussion in Confluence (dedicated-capacity-readiness-slo) and what we think we can achieve with automation + gating.

Target outcome (initial):
- 80% of runs Ready within 8h
- 95% of runs Ready within 16h

Proposed stage budgets (p50 targets) + alerts (stuck thresholds)
- Provisioning
  - target p50: <= 1h 30m
  - stuck alert: > 3h (ticket), > 5h (page)
- Imaging
  - target p50: <= 2h
  - stuck alert: > 4h (ticket), > 8h (page)
- Bootstrapping
  - target p50: <= 1h
  - stuck alert: > 2h (ticket), > 4h (page)
- Validating
  - target p50: <= 45m
  - stuck alert: > 90m (ticket), > 2h (page)

Notes:
- “Ticket vs page” needs final agreement with SRE (see ongoing discussion in #eng-sre 1708712222).
- These thresholds are intentionally conservative to reduce noise while we harden instrumentation.

Data quality notes / gaps
- We need standardized stage events with correlation IDs to avoid manual stitching.
  - This is the core deliverable in ENG-2748 (“Emit stage timing metrics and structured events; correlation IDs”).
- Missing in baseline:
  - explicit retries count per stage
  - “pause/resume” time accounting (human-imposed waiting)
  - consistent perf-canary execution (some runs used a lightweight smoke test only)

Recommendations (what to prioritize in automation)
Ranked by expected p95 impact reduction.

1) Imaging robustness and locality
- Add region-aware artifact sources + fallback mirror (or prewarm)
- Ensure retries have bounded exponential backoff + surfacing of “mirror slow” as a distinct error category
- Make image versioning explicit and pinned per pool config; avoid “latest” behavior

2) Provisioning preflight checks
- Validate quotas before terraform apply
- Validate IAM permissions / role existence and emit actionable errors
- Enforce required variables + environment conventions early (lint step)

3) Bootstrap determinism via pinned versions
- Pin helm chart versions + values schema
- Validate helm values against schema/policy before apply
- Reduce “it depends on operator machine state” by moving all actions to orchestrated runs

4) Validation gates as first-class, but keep them bounded
- GPU health check should be automated and result in clean remediation guidance (replace node) rather than ambiguous failure
- Perf-canary readiness suite should output a compact JSON summary that control plane can store + display (pass/fail + key numbers)

Open questions
- Should expansions have a different SLO from brand new pools?
  - Today expansions are generally faster (median 4h 25m) but can still hit imaging tail.
- What is the correct “Ready” semantic for routing?
  - Platform discussion suggests only advertise when Validating fully passes; do not treat “Validating” as usable capacity.
- How do we account for intentional waits (customer maintenance window) vs automation delays?
  - We likely need a “PausedByOperator” state (and subtract from SLO) with audit logs.

Next steps
- Align stage budgets + alerting thresholds with SRE (Rafael/Aisha) and Platform (Ethan/Ravi).
- Once structured events ship (ENG-2748), rerun this analysis with real metrics and extend sample size to 30+ runs.
- Add a “delay cause taxonomy” to events (quota, iam, mirror, helm-values, gpu-health, dns/tls, etc.) so we can track top issues without manual log review.

Appendix A: quick stats by run type
- New pools (n=6):
  - p50 total: 10h 15m
  - primary tail: Imaging + Bootstrapping
- Expansions (n=4):
  - p50 total: 4h 25m
  - primary tail: Imaging (when it happens)

Appendix B: notes on individual problem runs
- R-2416 (us-east-1, A100): Imaging had repeated timeouts; operator manually retried with alternate artifact path; ~8h lost.
- R-2418 (eu-central-1, H100): Bootstrapping stuck due to helm values misconfig; required manual rollback + re-apply; escalated to incident-style thread.
- R-2420 (us-east-1, A100 expansion): Imaging retries + intentional pause while confirming customer window; we need explicit pause accounting in the state machine.
